proof_summary: Take the counterexample \(n=33085221781504=2^{14}\cdot4409\cdot458009\), where both odd factors are prime. Rewriting the divisor-deficiency sum as \(a(n)=2\sigma(n)-\sum_{d\mid n}\sigma(d)\), multiplicativity and the prime-power formulas give \(\sigma(n)=66183576284700\) and \(\sum_{d\mid n}\sigma(d)=132367152569399\), so \(a(n)=1\) although \(n\ne1,12\).
